note:
**The meaning of the verses**
When Talut set out with his soldiers to fight the Amalekites, he said to them: "Allah is going to test your patience with a river in front of you that you will cross, so that the believer may be told apart from the hypocrite. Whoever of you drinks from the river's water is not of my religion and is not fit to strive with me; and whoever does not taste the water is of me, because he obeys my command and is fit to strive — except whoever takes the allowance and scoops one handful with his hand; there is no blame on him." When they reached the river, they threw themselves on the water and drank too much of it, except a small number of them who were patient with thirst and heat and made do with a handful, … Those who were certain of meeting Allah answered, reminding their brothers of Allah and His power, saying: "How many a small group of patient believers has overcome, by Allah's permission and command, a large group of disbelieving oppressors! And Allah is with the patient, with His help, His victory and His good reward."

When they came out to face Jalut and his soldiers and saw the danger with their own eyes, they turned to Allah in du'a and humble pleading, saying: "Our Lord, pour great patience upon our hearts, make our feet firm and steady in fighting the enemy so that they do not flee from the terror of war, and give us victory, with Your help and support, over the disbelieving people."

So they defeated them by Allah's permission, and Dawud, peace be upon him, killed Jalut, the leader of the tyrants. After that, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave Dawud kingship and prophethood among the Children of Israel, …

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What was the test at the river? And who passed it? (The water was not forbidden to them, and they were allowed a handful; it was their leader's command, so that it would be known who was patient and obedient.)
2. When some of them saw Jalut's army, they said: ﴿لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ﴾ (We have no power today against Jalut and his soldiers). How did those who knew they would meet Allah answer them?
3. What du'a did they make before they met the enemy? And why did they ask for patience before victory?

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child chooses something they love and puts it off (sweets until after the meal, or playing until after homework), and says their du'a to themselves: ﴿رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا﴾ (Our Lord, pour patience upon us). At the end of the week, count together how many times they were patient.
